Bounded parent read-only facts now available in finish-direct-isolation3-status1.json and finish-direct-isolation3-live-observations1.json. Final public status: A ready/live, B starting/nonready. Under existing final State noncreating/nonwaiting transaction, selected ProcessIdentity.runner_matches? validates both exact launch runners; all14 currently recorded child tuples match for each. Both processes.complete=false while live is normal; no exit/cleanup inference. Parent observation uses named PID reads only, no source/runtime mutation.
Genuine K68 source is /nix/store/r1b23g240p4yr44f5qgh3zhaj89qjmy0-source. Its resume179 reads accepted-artifact.json; initial reader refusal may precede its acceptance. Please verify accepted-artifact existence/contract from safe retained record facts, not values containing configuration. The finite campaign has an incomplete attempt and its own no-replay rule; any supported continuation must account for that separately, not manually finalize source/readiness or delete attempt.
Also found a diagnostic qualification: the finite wrapper recorded_live_tuples comparison uses uid/exe keys, while actual K ProcessIdentity receipts use owner_uid/executable, so those historical measurement tuple arrays supplied no match proof. Reserve/RAM/shm monitoring and controller/verifier unit admission are independent and worked. Current named SDK observations supply fresh proof, not retroactive history. Do not attribute B refusal to this observation defect.
If exact K68 cannot be recovered through supported public contracts, consider whether a genuine already-published historical baseline with the atomic reader correction (not fabricated/patched K68) can supply meaningful real old-to-new runtime evidence, with explicit differences/limits including unchanged V. This is consultation only, not permission to switch acceptance or launch anything. We should avoid repeated probability-based attempts or a new recovery framework solely for test acceptance.
